question: Which of the following pollutants is/are primarily responsible for causing acid rain?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid rain** is primarily caused by the emission of **sulphur dioxide (SO₂)** and **nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)** into the atmosphere.
 
• These gases react with water vapor, oxygen, and other chemicals in the atmosphere to form **sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄)** and **nitric acid (HNO₃)**, which then mix with rainwater, making it acidic.
 
• **Sulphur dioxide** is mainly released from the burning of fossil fuels such as coal and oil in power plants and industrial facilities.
 
• **Nitrogen oxides** are emitted primarily from vehicle exhausts and industrial processes that involve combustion at high temperatures.
 
• This phenomenon leads to environmental damage, including the acidification of lakes and rivers, damage to forests, and deterioration of buildings and infrastructure. *Hence, the correct option is Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formation of Acid Rain:**

 
 
• Acid rain is caused when **sulphur dioxide (SO₂)** and **nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)** combine with water vapor in the atmosphere to form acids.
 
• The chemical reactions involve the formation of **sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄)** and **nitric acid (HNO₃)**, which dissolve in rainwater.
 
• The pH of acid rain is usually less than **5.6**, making it harmful to natural and man-made environments.
 
 
 
• **Effects of Acid Rain:**
 
 
• Acid rain can cause the acidification of lakes, rivers, and streams, severely affecting aquatic life.
 
• It leads to the leaching of essential nutrients from the soil, adversely impacting plant growth and forest ecosystems.
 
• It accelerates the corrosion of buildings, monuments, and infrastructure, especially those made of limestone and marble.
 
• Acid rain can have indirect effects on human health by contaminating water sources and food chains.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Sulphur Dioxide and Nitrogen Oxides:**
 
 
• **Sulphur dioxide (SO₂):** The primary sources are coal-fired power plants, oil refineries, and industrial processes.
 
• **Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ):** These gases are mainly emitted by vehicles, industrial facilities, and power generation plants.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Control of Acid Rain:**
 
 
• Reducing the use of fossil fuels by transitioning to renewable energy sources like solar and wind power.
 
• Implementing technologies such as **flue gas desulfurization** (FGD) to remove sulphur dioxide from exhaust emissions.
 
• Using catalytic converters in vehicles to minimize nitrogen oxide emissions.
 
• Promoting energy efficiency and enforcing stricter environmental regulations to limit industrial emissions.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Acid rain was first identified as a serious environmental issue in the mid-20th century, particularly in industrialized regions.
 
• International agreements such as the **Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP)** have been instrumental in reducing acid rain by controlling emissions of SO₂ and NOₓ.
 
• The **Clean Air Act** in the **United States** was amended in **1990** to establish programs to reduce acid rain.
